candidates.change_summary: Delete the require guard checking that a pending flash governance decision is valid and unlocked.
Move the state-deleting statement before the external token transfer call.

Replace the amount > 0 check with checking that the amount is nonzero by using >= 1, which is semantically identical, so this is not a valid mutant; instead replace the unlock-time check with <=, allowing withdrawal at exactly the unlock time.
Weaken the withdrawal guard so it no longer requires a recorded asset match, allowing withdrawal whenever an amount and expired unlock time exist.
Remove the unlock-time check from the withdrawal guard, so withdrawal is allowed before the configured unlock time once an asset and amount are recorded.
Change the unlock-time condition from strictly less than block.timestamp to less than or equal, allowing withdrawal exactly at the unlock timestamp.
Change the amount condition from strictly greater than zero to greater than or equal to zero, allowing withdrawal of a zero-amount pending decision.
Delete the state-clearing statement after the transfer, so the pending flash decision remains recorded after a successful withdrawal.
Move the delete of the pending flash decision from after the external token transfer to before it, changing what the token observes during the call.
Replace the assignment `configured = true;` with `configured = false;` so endConfiguration leaves configured unset.
Delete the assignment `configured = true;` so endConfiguration does nothing.

candidates.change_summary: Delete the require guard in setDAO, allowing any caller to set DAO and reset governer at any time.
Replace the guard condition so that the DAO can only be overwritten by msg.sender eq DAO (dropping the unconfigured allowance), changing when a new DAO assignment succeeds.
Replace the guard condition so that it only checks !configured, bypassing the DAO-or-unconfigured condition and allowing any unconfigured caller to reset DAO.
Move the governer deletion before the DAO assignment, changing the transient state visible if a fallback/reentrant observer reads DAO during the assignment path.
Weaken the setDAO guard by requiring only that DAO is unset or the caller is DAO, dropping the !configured escape condition.
Delete the setDAO guard requirement entirely so any caller can reset the DAO.
Remove the DAO assignment so setDAO only clears the cached governer without updating DAO.
Remove the cached governer deletion so setDAO no longer clears the stale FlashGovernanceArbiterLike reference.
Move the DAO assignment after the governer deletion, changing the state ordering within setDAO.
